mcq.q: Which of the following is NOT a required property of an algorithm?
mcq.e: An algorithm must produce at least one output, so producing no output is not a property.

mcq.q: An algorithm's instructions must be clear and unambiguous. Which property is this?
mcq.e: Definiteness means each instruction is clear and unambiguous. Finiteness is about termination.

mcq.q: Which property says an algorithm must terminate after a finite number of instructions in all cases?
mcq.e: Finiteness requires termination after finitely many steps.

mcq.q: Space complexity of an algorithm refers to:
o: The running time of the algorithm
The amount of memory required to execute it
mcq.e: Space complexity is memory needed; running time is time complexity.

mcq.q: Which statement about randomised algorithms is correct?
o: Las Vegas algorithms may give wrong answers but run in fixed time
Las Vegas algorithms always give the correct output, but running time depends on the randomiser
Monte Carlo algorithms always give correct output with variable time
Las Vegas algorithms do not depend on a randomiser for execution time
mcq.e: Las Vegas: guaranteed correct answer, variable time. Monte Carlo is the mirror: fixed (polynomial) time, possible error.

mcq.q: Algorithms that always run in polynomial time but may return erroneous answers are called:
mcq.e: Monte Carlo algorithms trade correctness for guaranteed time.

mcq.q: Which traversal explores as far as possible along each branch before backtracking?
mcq.e: DFS goes deep then backtracks (stack); BFS goes level by level (queue).

mcq.q: Which of these is a subprogram?
mcq.e: Subprograms include both functions and subroutines.

mcq.q: In computational thinking, which skill does efficiently solving a Sudoku rest on most?
mcq.e: Sudoku solving relies mainly on pattern recognition.

mcq.q: Which flowchart symbol represents a decision?
mcq.e: A diamond denotes a decision/branch; the rectangle is process.

mcq.q: In a flowchart, a parallelogram is used for:
mcq.e: Parallelogram = input/output; oval = start/end.

mcq.q: Which flowchart symbol is used to link one part of a flowchart with another?
mcq.e: The circle is the connector symbol.

mcq.q: Among algorithm, flowchart and pseudocode, which is the easiest to transform into a computer program?
mcq.e: Pseudocode is written in code-like plain language, so it converts most easily.

mcq.q: Which statement about the sequence control construct is correct?
o: Statements may execute in any order
Each statement is executed once, in written order, with none repeated
Statements are repeated until a condition fails
mcq.e: Sequence = once each, in order. Repetition is loop; branching is selection.

mcq.q: Which of the following is NOT true of a compiler?
o: It translates source code into object code
It reads the entire source program
It reads and executes the program line by line
It is not involved in program execution
mcq.e: Line-by-line translation and execution is an interpreter's behaviour.

mcq.q: Which tool translates and executes a program one statement at a time?
mcq.e: An interpreter translates and executes each statement one at a time.

mcq.q: In the translation pipeline, which component places the executable in memory for execution?
mcq.e: Compiler gives object code, linker makes an executable, loader puts it in memory.

mcq.q: In the compiler phases, the semantic analyser gathers type information and saves it in the syntax tree or:
mcq.e: Type information is stored in the symbol table for intermediate code generation.

mcq.q: Which of the following is an assembler directive rather than an executable instruction?
mcq.e: DB, ORG and END are directives; MOV is an executable instruction.

mcq.q: Which statement about macros is FALSE?
o: A macro name is used as an operation mnemonic
Macro calls are replaced by the macro body at assembly time
A macro is invoked by writing its name with required parameters
The macro definition also appears in the expanded source code
mcq.e: The definition is consumed; only the expansions appear in the expanded source.

mcq.q: Which statement about machine language is FALSE?
mcq.e: Machine language is hard to modify.

mcq.q: Prolog is an example of which generation of languages?
mcq.e: Prolog (and LISP) belong to 5GL, logic and AI languages.

mcq.q: Which statement about system software is FALSE?
o: It plays a vital role in the effective functioning of the system
It is typically written in low-level language
It is written in a high-level language
Application software is written in high-level languages
mcq.e: System software is typically written in low-level language.

mcq.q: What happens to automatic variables in each call of a recursive function?
o: They keep values from the previous call
They are initialised afresh in each call
They are shared among all calls
mcq.e: Each call gets a new activation record, so nothing carries over unless static is used.
mcq.t: 4.5 Variables, Data Types, Scope and Recursion

mcq.q: Which statement about an external (global) variable is true?
o: It is initialised to 0 by default
It is accessible only in the function that declares it
It cannot be declared with extern in other functions
It is destroyed when any function returns
mcq.e: External variables are global, declared with extern elsewhere, and default to 0.
mcq.t: 4.5 Variables, Data Types, Scope and Recursion

mcq.q: A run-time error gives rise to a condition called:
mcq.e: A run-time error such as divide by zero raises an exception.

mcq.q: Loading a program with print statements to reveal the faulty statement is which debugging method?
mcq.e: Print-statement debugging is the brute force method.

tf.s: An algorithm is dependent on the programming language in which it is coded.
tf.n: False: an algorithm is language independent.

tf.s: Algorithms are easy to debug because their steps are precise.
tf.n: Precise steps make correctness easy to check.

tf.s: Efficiency of an algorithm is measured in terms of time and space.
Top-down design order is: analyse the problem, write the main module, write remaining modules, connect modules, revise and resequence.
tf.n: This is the stated top-down order.

tf.s: fork() and join() together make a complete process subroutine.
A diamond-based branch in a flowchart represents the decision structure.
A compiler reads the source program line by line.
tf.n: False: a compiler reads the entire source program.
Each assembly language is tied to a machine.
False: JIT is Just-In-Time, compiling intermediate language to machine language before execution.

tf.s: BASIC is an interactive language, and C is typically compiled.
tf.n: BASIC is interactive; C is compiled while Perl is interpreted.

tf.s: A pseudo-instruction is given to the assembler.
A variable has a storage location and a data type.
tf.n: These are essentials of a variable.

tf.s: A namespace in C++ defines a scope for identifiers.
A syntax error is caught at compile time.
tf.n: Syntax errors are grammar violations found at compile time.

tf.s: A semantic (logic) error crashes the program at compile time.
tf.n: False: it is legal code with wrong meaning, giving wrong output without a crash.

tf.s: Software package is a set of computer programs with the necessary documentation.
